name: Chandler Davis
bio: Horace Chandler Davis was a University of Michigan mathematician fired by the university and convicted of contempt of Congress for refusing, on First Amendment grounds, to answer the House Un-American Activities Committee. In December 1959 the Supreme Court declined to review his case, leaving him to serve a six-month sentence.
charges: Contempt of Congress — refusing to answer HUAC on First Amendment grounds
convicted: Convicted; Supreme Court refused review December 1959

name: Sidney Turoff
bio: Sidney Turoff was convicted of contempt of Congress by a federal jury in Buffalo in December 1959 for refusing to give the House Un-American Activities Committee the names of members of an alleged Communist Party 'steel section.'
charges: Contempt of Congress — refusing to name alleged Communists to HUAC
convicted: Convicted by a Buffalo federal jury (1959)

name: Ruth Bishop
bio: Ruth Bishop was a California teacher subpoenaed in the 1959 House Un-American Activities Committee probe of public-school teachers. After she flung the subpoena — and a broom — at the process server, she was indicted on three counts of 'force and violence' and found guilty by a Long Beach jury, paying a fine to avoid 60 days in jail.
charges: 'Force and violence' against a process server — resisting a HUAC subpoena
convicted: Found guilty by a Long Beach jury (1959)
sentence: Fined (in lieu of 60 days in jail)

name: Karl Meyer
bio: Karl Meyer was a 22-year-old Catholic Worker pacifist (son of Rep. William H. Meyer of Vermont) who took part in 'Omaha Action,' the 1959 civil-disobedience campaign against the Mead, Nebraska intercontinental ballistic missile base. Arrested for trespassing, he had his probation revoked and was sentenced to six months and a $500 fine; he had also been arrested repeatedly in New York for refusing compulsory civil-defense drills.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Mead, Nebraska ICBM missile base
sentence: Six months in jail and a $500 fine

name: Ross Anderson
bio: Ross Anderson, 59, of Americus, Georgia, was one of the pacifists who in July 1959 climbed the fence at the Mead, Nebraska Atlas missile base with A. J. Muste in the 'Omaha Action' protest against nuclear weapons, and was arrested for trespassing.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Mead, Nebraska ICBM missile base

name: Wilmer Young
bio: Wilmer Young, a 71-year-old Quaker of Wallingford, Pennsylvania, was arrested for trespassing in July 1959 when he walked to the gate of the Mead, Nebraska intercontinental missile base in the 'Omaha Action' campaign of nonviolent protest against nuclear weapons.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Mead, Nebraska ICBM missile base

name: Dave Wyland
bio: Dave Wyland, 23, of Toledo, Ohio, was one of the 'Omaha Action' pacifists who climbed over the fence at the Mead, Nebraska Atlas missile base in July 1959 to protest nuclear weapons, and was arrested for trespassing.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Mead, Nebraska ICBM missile base

name: Bradford Lyttle
bio: Bradford Lyttle was a pacifist organizer of 'Omaha Action,' the 1959 nonviolent campaign against the Mead, Nebraska intercontinental ballistic missile base. Arrested for trespassing and disregarding a court order, he was sentenced to six months in jail and a $500 fine.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Mead, Nebraska ICBM missile base
sentence: Six months in jail and a $500 fine

name: Donald Fortenberry
bio: Donald Fortenberry was a pacifist arrested with Bradford Lyttle in July 1959 for trespassing at the Mead, Nebraska missile base during the 'Omaha Action' protest against nuclear weapons; he was sentenced to six months in jail and a $500 fine.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Mead, Nebraska ICBM missile base
sentence: Six months in jail and a $500 fine

name: Ed Lazar
bio: Ed Lazar, a 24-year-old New York City pacifist, was jailed for six months for antinuclear civil disobedience at the Mead, Nebraska intercontinental missile base in the July 1959 'Omaha Action' campaign.
charges: Trespassing — antinuclear protest at the Mead, Nebraska ICBM missile base

name: Arthur Harvey
bio: Arthur Harvey was one of a group of pacifists arrested in New York City in April 1959 for refusing to take shelter during the compulsory 'Operation Alert' civil-defense drill — a protest against preparations for nuclear war. He chose to serve jail time rather than pay the fine.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a compulsory civil-defense drill (New York Defense Emergency Act)
sentence: Jailed rather than pay the fine

name: David McReynolds
bio: David McReynolds, editor of the pacifist magazine Liberation and later a leading figure in the War Resisters League, was among those arrested in New York City in April 1959 for refusing to take shelter during the compulsory civil-defense drill, invoking the Nuremberg principles in his protest against nuclear-war preparations.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a compulsory civil-defense drill (New York Defense Emergency Act)
sentence: Arrested for the antinuclear civil-defense protest
